thread:
Aditi (SRE): Pager fired: multiple 504s to Vela Systems (dedicated pool eu-west-2). Error pattern looks like backend connect failures, manifests starting ~09:03 UTC.
Tom (on-call): I'm on it, grabbing logs. pinging infra nodes.
inc-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-3312345678. Pager escalated to #incidents -> on-call.
Aditi (SRE): quick notes — affected routes: /v1/infer (model: rdx-large-16q). Latency spiked then 504s. No rolling deploys in last 30m per deploy-bot.
deploy-bot: No active deploys in last 60m.
Tom (on-call): Can confirm CPU/GPU nodes show high connection resets to redis-kvcache-3. tcp retransmits high. Attaching sample netstat:```
ESTABLISHED 10.0.12.7:443 10.0.5.12:53245
SYN_SENT 10.0.12.7:443 10.0.5.12:53250
RST 10.0.12.7:443 10.0.5.13:53251
```
Jia (ENG-MGR): thx. Are customers impacted? Which enterprise accounts see errors? Priya pls pull contact list.
Priya (Acct Exec): Vela Systems (acct_id VELA-001) reporting 20% error rate on their flows; also note AltoTech (ALTO-22) has a handful of errors but not full outage. Vela is the big one. I have primary contacts: 
- +44 7700 900111 (Elena, Platform Ops)
- vela-oncall@vela-sys.com (pager)
- Raj (CISO) - raj@vela-sys.com
I can draft a short customer notification.
Aditi (SRE): Good. We'll need an immediate status page update and customer-safe wording. Keep it factual: onset, impact, mitigation actions, ETA if possible.
Tom (on-call): Mitigation steps I'm running now: 1) restart kvcache-3 on node group B (graceful) 2) temporarily route Vela traffic to eu-west-1 fallback pool 3) enable increased connection backoff on proxy. Applying step 1 now.
Miles (Support): prepping a support DM template for Vela's support channel.
Tom (on-call): restart succeeded on kvcache-3, connections stabilized -> seeing drop in 504s to some sessions. But overall error rate for Vela still ~8% (down from 20%).
Aditi (SRE): Good. Keep fallback routing as an option, only if errors persist after warmup.
Priya (Acct Exec): Draft customer note v1 below — please review/trim.
```
Subject: Service disruption affecting Vela Systems — temporary request errors

Hi Elena / Vela team,

We're investigating intermittent 504 errors impacting inference requests in your dedicated region (eu-west-2) starting ~09:03 UTC. Our engineers have identified connection instability between our proxy layer and a KV cache node serving your pool and are applying mitigations.

Impact: ~20% of requests initially failing; partial recovery in progress. Some requests may still receive 504s or increased latency.
What we're doing: attempting node restart, warming a fallback pool in eu-west-1, and temporarily adjusting routing to reduce failures.
ETA: initial mitigation has reduced errors; we expect continued improvements over the next 30–60 minutes. We will update again within 15 minutes or sooner if anything changes.

Contact: Priya (Acct) — priya@redwood.ai, Aditi (SRE) — aditi@redwood.ai

Sorry for the disruption.
```
Jia (ENG-MGR): LGTM. Remove internal commentary. Keep ETA conservative: "30–60 mins" is fine.
Aditi (SRE): Also prepare an internal status page snippet for ops/status. Use this short text:```
Incident: Elevated 5xx rates for Vela Systems (dedicated eu-west-2)
Status: Mitigating — node restart applied; fallback routing warming in eu-west-1
Impact: Some requests may return 504 or increased latency.
Mitigation: Restarted KV cache node; optionally routing traffic to fallback pool.
Next update: in 15 minutes
```
Tom (on-call): Running the routing switch as scheduled to fallback pool now for Vela only (`route-set --customer VELA-001 --to eu-west-1-fallback --weight 100`). Will monitor.
inc-bot: Handoff reminder — Tom is shifting to 30m watch, set a follow-up timer for 15m.
Tom (on-call): After routing switch, Vela error rate dropped to ~1.5% almost baseline. Rolling acceptance tests show normal token throughput.
Miles (Support): Sending the customer note to Elena via email and DMing the oncall pager. Using the template approved.
Priya (Acct Exec): Sent. Elena replied: "Appreciate the quick action. We'll monitor on our side. Please keep us posted." :thumbsup:
Jia (ENG-MGR): Good customer response. Please prepare a short internal comms template for execs and CSMs so they can notify stakeholders. 
Aditi (SRE): Internal exec-ready blurb (one-paragraph):```
Brief: Between 09:03–09:20 UTC we observed elevated 5xx errors for the Vela Systems dedicated pool in eu-west-2 due to a KV cache node connection instability. We applied a node restart and temporarily routed traffic to a warmed fallback pool in eu-west-1. Error rates have returned to near baseline (~1–2%). No data loss detected. Next steps: full post-incident log collection and RCA.
```
Jia (ENG-MGR): Perfect. Miles, please stash that in the incident folder and circulate to CSMs.
Miles (Support): Done — uploaded notes and customer email to the incident doc link: https://redwood.internal/incidents/3312345678 (private).
Aditi (SRE): Marking incident as mitigated in the ticket but keeping it active for postmortem artifacts. Please capture timeline & config diff for KV cache cluster.
Tom (on-call): I'll hand this to night oncall in 45m. Leave the status page in "monitoring" state for now.
inc-bot: Incident INC-2026-3312345678 status changed: Mitigated -> Monitoring.
Priya (Acct Exec): Follow-up action for account team: plan a proactive call with Vela to review resilience options (multi-region pools, stronger health checks). I'll schedule for tomorrow.
Jia (ENG-MGR): Thanks team. After PMR, Ops please include the rollback plan and automation that failed health detection.
Aditi (SRE): Noted. Collecting logs now. I'll open the RFC for cache health-check improvements.
Tom (on-call): Handoff to night oncall done at 09:52 UTC. Leaving a short runbook in the incident doc. Good job everyone. :tada:
